note: Practice pack: 11+ vocabulary tasks with fixed answers. Generic content - contains no personal information.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to waste money or time when you really shouldn't'?
tasks.teach: To squander pocket money is to blow it all in one go — the show-off opposite of saving.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to tempt someone with something lovely'?
tasks.teach: The smell of warm cookies can entice anyone into the kitchen. Tempt, attract, entice — all magnets!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to officially say NO to a plan'?
tasks.teach: 'Permit' means allow — veto is its bossy opposite: one powerful NO that blocks the plan.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to stop completely'?
tasks.teach: When rain ceases, it stops. 'Cease' is a posh full stop — and 'commence' kicks things off.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'a huge, noisy crowd'?
tasks.teach: A horde of fans mobbed the stage! (Sneaky cousin: 'hoard' with an A is treasure you keep.)

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to keep going through something hard without giving up'?
tasks.teach: Explorers endure freezing nights — they grit their teeth and carry on. You endure a very long queue!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'looking down and feeling gloomy'?
tasks.teach: Downcast eyes stare at shoes. 'Jaunty' is the happy opposite — chin up, cap at an angle!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to get in the way and slow someone down'?
tasks.teach: A pebble in your shoe hinders a runner. Its rhyme-twin 'hamper' means exactly the same!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to run with quick little steps, like a squirrel'?
tasks.teach: Squirrels scamper, tired hikers trudge. The word sounds as quick as the feet!

tasks.prompt: A 'cryptic' message is...
tasks.teach: Cryptic = puzzling, hidden. To decipher a cryptic note is to crack its code — detective work!

tasks.prompt: Your 'visage' is your...
tasks.teach: A knight's grim visage = his stern face. Fancy word, simple meaning — examiners love it.

tasks.prompt: The sky turned a brilliant ___ over the summer sea.
tasks.teach: Azure = bright sky-blue. A painter's word — it makes a sentence glow.

tasks.prompt: The old oak's ___ branches twisted like a witch's fingers.
tasks.teach: Gnarled = twisted and knobbly. Perfect for old trees, old roots, and wizard's hands.

tasks.prompt: Which word is the odd one out?
tasks.teach: Cease, halt and stop all slam the brakes — commence starts the engine!

tasks.prompt: If you 'smell a rat', you...
tasks.teach: No actual rats involved! This idiom means 'something fishy is going on'. (Also fishy — English, honestly!)

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to give way or give in'?
tasks.teach: To yield is to give way — a car yields at a junction. (It also means to produce: a field yields crops.)

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'one level of several stacked up'?
tasks.teach: A tier is one layer in a stack — a three-tier cake, or the tiers of seats in a stadium.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'gentle — not strong or harsh'?
tasks.teach: Mild weather is soft and gentle; a mild curry won't burn your tongue.

tasks.prompt: A large group of fish moving together is a ___.
tasks.teach: Fish swim in a shoal, birds fly in a flock, bees buzz in a swarm — collect the group words!

tasks.prompt: After the storm, the sea began to ___ into huge waves.
tasks.teach: To swell is to grow bigger — a river swells after rain, and the sea swells into waves.

tasks.prompt: She is taller ___ her brother. (comparing two things)
tasks.teach: 'Than' compares two things (bigger than). 'Then' is about time — first this, then that.

tasks.prompt: Take a deep ___ and relax. (the air you take in)
tasks.teach: 'Breath' (rhymes with death) is the air — a naming word. 'Breathe' (rhymes with seethe) is the action.

tasks.prompt: Don't ___ off the path — you'll get lost! (to roam)
tasks.teach: 'Wander' (rhymes with ponder) means to roam about. 'Wonder' means to think or to be amazed.

tasks.prompt: She had ___ amazing idea!
tasks.teach: Use 'an' before a vowel sound: an apple, an amazing idea. Use 'a' before a consonant: a book.

tasks.prompt: Which one shows the wings belonging to ONE dragon?
tasks.teach: One dragon owning something takes 's — the dragon's wings. (No apostrophe just means MORE than one dragon.)

tasks.prompt: Which sentence is joined correctly?
options: It was raining. so we stayed inside.
It was raining, we stayed inside.
It was raining we stayed inside.
It was raining, so we stayed inside.
tasks.answer: It was raining, so we stayed inside.
tasks.teach: Two whole sentences can't be glued with just a comma — pop a joining word (so, and, but) after it.

tasks.prompt: When 'she said' splits the speech, which is correct?
tasks.teach: Comma inside the first speech marks, another after 'said', then reopen the speech marks for the rest.

tasks.prompt: ___ did you put my shoes? (asking about a place)
tasks.teach: 'Where' asks about a place — it has 'here' hiding inside it. 'Were' is a doing word: they were happy.
